(a) Maintenance Fee.—Section 4(i)(1) of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (7 U.S.C. 136a–1(i)(1)) is amended—
        (1) in subparagraph (C), by striking “an aggregate amount of $27,800,000 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “an average amount of $31,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”; 
        (2) in subparagraph (D)—
            (A) in clause (i), by striking “$115,500 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “$129,400 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”; and 
            (B) in clause (ii), by striking “$184,800 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “$207,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”;  
        (3) in subparagraph (E)(i)—
            (A) in subclause (I), by striking “$70,600 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “$79,100 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”; and 
            (B) in subclause (II), by striking “$122,100 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “$136,800 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”; and  
        (4) in subparagraph (I), by striking “2017..” and inserting “2023.”.  
    (b) Prohibition on Other Fees.—Section 4(i)(2) of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (7 U.S.C. 136a–1(i)(2)) is amended—
        (1) by striking “the date of enactment of this section and ending on September 30, 2019” and inserting “the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Extension Act of 2018 and ending on September 30, 2025”; and 
        (2) by inserting after “registration of a pesticide under this Act” the following: “or any other action covered under a table specified in section 33(b)(3),”.  
    (c) Extension of Prohibition on Tolerance Fees.—Section 408(m)(3) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 346a(m)(3)) is amended by striking “2017” and inserting “2023”.

fable.w: The section only amends pesticide maintenance fee amounts, fiscal-year ranges, and the duration of prohibitions on other fees and tolerance fees. The tempting reading is that fees paid by registrants, or the reference to registration actions, involve outside parties in a federal decision, but paying fees or applying for registration is not consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking authority, or a right to sue. No outside party is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Extension of Prohibition on Tolerance Fees

qwen_block.w: This section solely amends statutory text to update maintenance fee amounts and prohibition dates for pesticide registrations. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public hearing, advisory committee, or coordination with outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes applications for licenses or fees associated with them from being considered participation.
qwen_block.s: Section 4(i)(1) of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (7 U.S.C. 136a–1(i)(1)) is amended— (1) in subparagraph (C), by striking “an aggregate amount of $27,800,000 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “an average amount of $31,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section amends the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA), which involves pesticide registration, it implicitly involves participation. However, the text itself only changes fee amounts and dates. It does not describe any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" and notes that applying for something is not participating. Setting the fee for a license application is part of the application process, not a participatory decision-making process involving outsiders.

opus.w: This section only updates maintenance fee amounts, extends deadlines, and widens a ban on other fees under FIFRA and the FFDCA. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. The word "action" may look procedural, but here it only defines which actions the fee ban covers; it creates no comment period, consultation, or other channel for outside input.
opus.s: by inserting after “registration of a pesticide under this Act” the following: “or any other action covered under a table specified in section 33(b)(3),”
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** One might read "any other action covered under a table specified in section 33(b)(3)" as a federal decision process that involves registrants. That reading fails: the amendment only widens a ban on other fees. It doesn't create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, consultation, or right to sue. Everything else in the section only changes dollar amounts and dates.

qwen_chat.w: The section only amends the amounts of fees and the duration of prohibitions on other fees. It does not require any consultation, comment period, or advisory process involving outside parties. Paying a fee is not participation in a decision.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Maintenance Fee.—Section 4(i)(1) of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (7 U.S.C. 136a–1(i)(1)) is amended— (1) in subparagraph (C), by striking “an aggregate amount of $27,800,000 for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017” and inserting “an average amount of $31,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023”;
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves fees paid by companies to the government, which might be seen as a form of interaction.
Resolution: The section only amends the amounts of fees and the duration of prohibitions on other fees. It does not require any consultation, comment period, or advisory process involving outside parties. Paying a fee is not participation in a decision.
